newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian officers seek release of 15 officials.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian officers seek release of 15 officials.

text.p: Top Cambodian military officers are in Thailand seeking the release of 15 men from the Khmer Rouge, a senior officer said on Monday.
The officer, General Long Sereirath, also said he had talked to one of the 15, a pilot, who told him all were well and hopeful about the negotiations.
The 15 have been in Anlong Veng district since February 14 when they flew by helicopter into the area to negotiate with Khmer Rouge commander Ta Mok about defecting.

The Khmer Rouge, whose 1975-79 rule left more than one million people dead, have been severely weakened by thousands of defections in the past six months and are now believed to number less than 2,000, mostly in Anlong Veng.

Long Sereirath, deputy military regional commander in the northwest province of Siem Reap, said by telephone that armed forces Deputy Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Nhiek Bun Chhay and regional military commander Major General Khan Savoeun were in Thailand on Sunday and Monday to negotiate with the rebels.

Long Sereirath said there had been hitches and that Ta Mok had put forward many conditions. The general did not say what these were, but said Nhiek Bun Chhay and Khan Savoeun had gone to Thailand to "discuss final conditions."
The Cambodian government has said it would soon tell Ta Mok to hand over the detained staff or face attack.
The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-sponsored peace pact in 1991, but reneged on the deal and have been fighting the coalition government which came to power after 1993 elections.
In a separate development, a local newsaper reported on Monday that the royalist FUNCINPEC party planned to appoint two controversial officials to provincial governships.
Cambodia Today said the party hoped to replace their governors in Kandal province, neighbouring Phnom Penh, and northwest Banteay Meanchey province with Serei Kosal and Prom Su respectively.

Serei Kosal was the deputy governor of the northwest province of Battambang until he and three other top officials were recalled last month following clashes between FUNCINPEC and its partner and main rival in the coalition, the Cambodian People's Party.
Prom Su, a relative of Nhiek Bun Chhay, was a former Khmer Rouge commander who defected to the government last year.
Analysts feared the appointments, if confirmed, could exacerbate strained relations between the two parties.
